brief: A kitchen herb planter: three bins on bases, filled with soil and planted with basil, thyme and mint.

requirements.evidence: Three bases (piece:0,0,0; piece:1,0,0; piece:1,-1,0, full hex) each hold a full-depth drained bin (bin:0,0,0, bin:1,0,0, bin:1,-1,0 ~hex-bin-full-drain). The bases are joined by joint bolts.
fill_and_plant filled soil in all three bins; check_build reports no PLANT_NOT_IN_SOIL or prop warnings.

requirements.requirement: Planted with basil, thyme and mint
requirements.evidence: basil-young in bin:0,0,0, thyme-young in bin:1,0,0, mint-young in bin:1,-1,0. Each bed is a young-stage plug plant.

Geometry and fit are verified (meshClash clear, zero issues). The configurator does not check food safety, material suitability, waterproofing or drainage performance; the bins have drain-style floors, but the chosen print material must be judged by the user.

finish.summary: Built a three-cell herb planter: three full hex bases joined by joint bolts, each with a full-depth drained bin, capped open faces, filled with soil, and planted with basil (back-left cell), thyme (east cell) and mint (north-east cell). check_build is clean with meshClash clear. Food safety and material durability were not and cannot be verified by the configurator.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
